previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of chronic left shoulder pain due to rotator cuff tears, SIADH, and aortic stenosis was admitted for severe worsening shoulder pain and a low sodium level of 118. Evaluation revealed septic arthritis of the left shoulder caused by Streptococcus viridans, confirmed by joint fluid analysis. He underwent open irrigation and debridement and was started on intravenous vancomycin, with a PICC line placed for long-term antibiotic therapy. During the hospitalization, he developed transient atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, which resolved spontaneously; he was started on warfarin with a heparin bridge for stroke prevention. His hyponatremia, attributed to SIADH exacerbated by pain, improved with fluid restriction. He remained afebrile with decreasing white blood cell count and was discharged to extended care for completion of a four-week antibiotic course, ongoing anticoagulation management, and rehabilitation.

Brief Hospital Course:
Assessment and Plan: This is a ___ yo man with left septic 
arthritis (strep virdans) in ___ s/p surgical debridement, on 
vancomycin who presented from rehab with erythema of left 
shoulder concerning for cellulitis, found to have strep 
bacteremia and possible early right shoulder septic arthritis.

# Bacteremia, strep viridans: From initial cultures in ED,

and orthopedics. He underwent bilateral arthrocentesis to 
evaluate for potential source of infection. His left shoulder 
did not appear infected. His right shoulder returned with 15,000

negative) but not entirely clear. Given this repeat 
arthrocentesis was done ___ and WBC improved to 1200, suggesting

initially treated with vancomycin given pcn allergy, however he 
was switched to ceftriaxone on ___ and tolerated this without

continue ceftriaxone through that appointment.  PICC was placed

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with cellulitis and shoulder pain.

FINDINGS:  Degenerative changes are identified at the left acromioclavicular
joint and left glenohumeral joint, without significant interval change since
prior radiograph ___.  Subarticular cysts are again identified at the
humeral head.  No obvious areas of gas are seen in the adjacent soft tissues.

INDICATION:  Left shoulder discomfort with overlying concern for cellulitis
with history of previous left septic joint, status post wash-out in early
___.

COMPARISON:  Shoulder radiograph from earlier on the same day as well as
radiographs from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial CT images were acquired through the left shoulder in the
absence of intravenous contrast.  Note the contrast was not administered per
patient request.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were also reviewed.

FINDINGS:  Hypodensity is visualized surrounding the left shoulder joint
consistent with an effusion.  Hypodensity is also visualized superior to the
humeral head, likely representing fluid in the subacromial and subdeltoid
bursa.  Enhancement characteristics of the wall of this effusion are not
assessed in the absence of intravenous contrast.  Bony erosions are visualized
in the acromion, clavicular head, humeral head and to a lesser degree in the
glenoid.  These findings appear new or progressed since ___, though are
similar to those seen on comparison radiograph and raise concern for
infectious related osteolysis.  The imaged portions of the left hemithorax are
notable for a left pleural effusion.  The portions of the heart reveal
extensive coronary arterial calcification.  A central line terminates at the
superior cavoatrial junction.  The remainder of the visualized skeleton is
unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  Left glenohumeral joint effusion as above.  Given the recent
history and current clinical presentation, this raises concern for possible
septic arthritis.  Also noted are underlying osseous erosive changes,
progressed from ___, but appearing similar to that seen recently, possibly
representing osteolysis related to septic arthritis.

AP CHEST 01:00 A.M. ON ___

HISTORY:  A ___ man with a PIC placement.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

The right PIC line ends in the region of the superior cavoatrial junction. 
Bilateral pleural effusion, small on the left, tiny on the right has
increased.  Borderline cardiomegaly is stable.  Mediastinal vasculature
borderline enlarged, no pulmonary edema.  Fullness in the upper mediastinum
probably due to tortuous head and neck vessels.

FLUOROSCOPIC-GUIDED ASPIRATION OF BILATERAL SHOULDER JOINTS

INDICATION:  History of strep viridans arthritis of left shoulder now
bacteremic, concern for recurrence of septic arthritis at left shoulder and
new right shoulder septic arthritis.

TECHNIQUE:  Written informed consent from the patient's next of kin was
obtained over the telephone by Dr. ___ Dr. ___.  The
procedure was performed with the assistance of an interpreter.  A preprocedure
timeout confirming patient identity, procedure side and site was performed.

A suitable position for aspiration of the right shoulder was marked in the
skin with fluoroscopic assistance.  The skin was prepped with Betadine.  1%
lidocaine was used to anesthetize the skin and subcutaneous tissues.  Under
intermittent fluoroscopic guidance, a 20-gauge spinal needle was advanced into
the right glenohumeral joint.  Approximately 6 cc of cloudy fluid was
aspirated.  This sample was sent for Gram stain, culture and sensitivity in
addition to cell count and differential.

A separate procedure was then performed to aspirate the left shoulder.  The
left shoulder was prepped with Betadine.  Under intermittent fluoroscopic
guidance, a 20-gauge spinal needle was advanced into the left glenohumeral
joint.  Approximately 6 cc of blood-stained fluid was aspirated from the left
shoulder joint.  This was sent for cell count and differential in addition to
Gram stain, culture and sensitivity.  The procedure was well tolerated.  

___, the attending physician, was present and available throughout
the procedure.

IMAGING FINDINGS:
Fluoroscopic images of the right shoulder demonstrate complete obliteration of
the acromiohumeral interval compatible with a full-thickness rotator cuff
tear.  Degenerative changes are seen at the right humeral head.  Injection of
contrast into the left glenohumeral joint demonstrated extension of contrast
through the left acromioclavicular joint compatible with extension of contrast
through rotator cuff tear into the subacromial/subdeltoid space and through
the acromiohumeral interval.  This is compatible with a full-thickness rotator
cuff tear.  There is also a complete effacement of the acromiohumeral interval
on the left.  There is abnormal lucency at the articular surface of the left
humerus unchanged from prior examination on ___.

IMPRESSION:  
1. Successful aspiration of fluid from bilateral shoulder joints and sample
sent separately for Gram stain, culture and sensitivity in addition to cell
count and differential from each shoulder.
2. Bilateral narrowing of acromio-humeral interval compatible with full-
thickness rotator cuff tears.

HISTORY:  ___ male with recently removed left arm PICC, now with
redness and tenderness in the left upper arm.  Left wrist peripheral IV in
place.  Here to assess for DVT in the left upper extremity.

COMPARISON:  None available.

LEFT UPPER EXTREMITY VENOUS ULTRASOUND:  Grayscale and color and pulse wave
Doppler examinations were performed over the right subclavian vein, and the
left internal jugular, subclavian, axillary, and brachial veins.  This study
demonstrates normal compressibility, venous waveforms with normal respiratory
variation, and augmentation.  No intraluminal thrombus is seen within these
deep veins.  Also normal color flow and compressibility are demonstrated in
the left basilic and cephalic veins.

In the antecubital region, which is not involved in the area of erythema and
pain, there is a well-circumscribed mildly lobulated ovoid 0.9 x 1.5 x 1.7 cm
lesion in the superficial subcutaneous soft tissues, which is predominantly
hypoechoic with central rounded area of mild echogenicity, and with posterior
wall enhancement and increased through transmission.  Color Doppler
interrogation demonstrates vessels along the edges of this lesion but not
within.  This lesion corresponds to a small soft visible and palpable nodule
on exam, which the patient reports has been present for the last two to ___
years.

IMPRESSIONS: 
1. No evidence of DVT seen in the left upper extremity. 
2. Incidental note of ovoid, slightly lobulated 1.7 cm long hypoechoic lesion
in the superficial subcutaneous soft tissues of the left antecubital region.
Given presence for two to ___ years and lack of surrounding erythema and
inflammation, abscess collection is less likely. Differential includes lipoma
or other subcutaneous soft tissue nodule. If clinically indicated, limited CT
could be performed through this region to confirm fat density.

HISTORY:  Strep viridans septic arthritis of the left shoulder.  Monitor a
white blood cell in the right shoulder.

COMPARISON:  Bilateral shoulder aspiration ___.

PROCEDURE:  Fluoroscopic-guided right shoulder joint aspiration.

Informed consent was previously obtained from the patient's son and repeat
informed consent was obtained from the patient with a ___ interpreter
present.  The skin over the right shoulder was prepped and draped in a sterile
fashion.  1% lidocaine was injected into the subcutaneous tissues for local
anesthetic.  A 20-gauge spinal needle was advanced into the right glenohumeral
joint under intermittent fluoroscopic observation.  Approximately 55 cc of
clear, yellow joint fluid was aspirated.  The joint fluid was sent for Gram
stain culture, and cell count.

No fluoroscopic images could be obtained due to malfunction of the fluoroscopy
device.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and was transported to his hospital
room.

The procedure was performed with and supervised by Dr. ___.

FINDINGS:

Initial scout fluoroscopic images of the right shoulder demonstrate
glenohumeral osteoarthritis with joint space loss and degenerative spurring.

IMPRESSION:
Successful right shoulder aspiration.  55 cc of clear, yellow joint fluid was
aspirated and sent for cell count and differential.

PICC LINE PLACEMENT
 
INDICATION: IV access needed for antibiotics.
 
The procedure was explained to the patient. A timeout was performed.
 
RADIOLOGIST: Dr. ___ performed the procedure.  Dr. ___, the
attending radiologist, reviewed the study.
 
TECHNIQUE: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right basilic
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access. A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guidewire and a single lumen PICC line measuring 37 cm in length was then
placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the SVC under
fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.
 
The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured
to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.
 
The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.
 
IMPRESSION: Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided ___
single lumen PICC line placement via the right basilic venous approach. Final
internal length is 37 cm with the tip positioned in SVC. The line is ready to
use.
